pageNodes.subtitle: A visual walkthrough of the content editor, the page tree, and the tools around them.

versions.content:
[{"kind":"region","layout":"single","columns":[[{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

This guide covers the content-management features that ship with Check performance data \u2014 how content pages, widgets, versions, blocks, and the page-tree admin work in practice.

Two parts, split by who does what:

  • For editors \u2014 authoring pages, choosing widgets, using content blocks, drafting and publishing.
  • For administrators \u2014 page-tree drag-and-drop, content staging (import / export), role-based access, and the in-app log viewer.

Screens shown throughout are captured from the current build against real seeded content \u2014 you should see the same elements in your environment.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Where to go next"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

For editors

Create a page, add widgets, draft, publish, manage versions, and use content blocks.

For administrators

Manage the page tree, import / export content, configure roles, view application logs.

"}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: How to use the CMS. Two parts: for editors and for administrators. Content pages, widgets, versions, blocks, page-tree admin, content staging, roles, logs.

Open the admin pages view"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

From the admin menu, choose CMS administration then Pages. The left-hand nav mirrors the public site: every folder and content page you can see in the tree here is the same one your visitors reach.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"2. Choose the parent"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Click into the page you want to be the parent. The action toolbar at the top of the pages screen has a + New child page icon. Right-click any node in the left nav for the same option (plus Edit, Versions, Delete).

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"3. Choose a page type"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Three page types are available:

  • Content \u2014 the widget-based editor. Use this for landing pages and long-form pages that benefit from a mix of headings, rich text, cards, and other widgets.
  • Wiki \u2014 a single rich-text body. Simpler; good for short reference pages.
  • Folder \u2014 a container that doesn't render on its own. Its child index renders instead. Use folders to group content without adding a landing page.
"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"4. Fill in the properties"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Title is the H1 of the rendered page. Segment is the URL slug \u2014 it defaults from the title but you can override it. PageName is an optional short label used in menus when the full title is too long. Subtitle appears above the H1 as a caption on content pages.

ShowInMenu is on by default. Turn it off to hide the page from menus and search widgets while keeping it live at its URL \u2014 handy for pages that are linked to from elsewhere but don't belong in the main navigation.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: 1. Open the admin pages view From the admin menu, choose CMS administration then Pages . The left-hand nav mirrors the public site: every folder and content page you can see in the tree here is the same one your visitors reach. The left nav shows every page in the tree. Right-click any node for actions. 2. Choose the parent Click into the page you want to be the parent. The action toolbar at the top of the pages screen has a + New child page icon. Right-click any node in the left nav for the same option (plus Edit, Versions, Delete). 3. Choose a page type Three page types are available: Content — the widget-based editor. Use this for landing pages and long-form pages that benefit from a mix of headings, rich text, cards, and other widgets. Wiki — a single rich-text body. Simpler; good for short reference pages. Folder — a container that doesn't render on its own. Its child index renders instead. Use folders to group content without adding a landing page. 4. Fill in the properties Title is the H1 of the rendered page. Segment is the URL slug — it defaults from the title but you can override it. PageName is an optional short label used in menus when the full title is too long. Subtitle appears above the H1 as a caption on content pages. ShowInMenu is on by default. Turn it off to hide the page from menus and search widgets while keeping it live at its URL — handy for pages that are linked to from elsewhere but don't belong in the main navigation. Properties tab: every attribute of the page in one form.

pageNodes.title: Editing with widgets

versions.content:
[{"kind":"region","layout":"one-third-two-thirds","columns":[[{"kind":"widget","type":"pagenav","props":{"mode":"children","childrenParentPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-editors","showSearch":false,"searchPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-editors","searchLabel":"Search this section"}}],[{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Content pages are built from a tree of regions containing widgets. A region is a horizontal band that can be split into columns; each column holds an ordered list of widgets.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"The editor at a glance"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Adding a widget"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Every gap between widgets shows an inline Add content here button. Click it to open the widget picker. The palette lists widgets alphabetically:

  • Card \u2014 title + body + optional image and link. Cards laid out in the same row auto-equalise height.
  • Divider \u2014 a horizontal rule.
  • Heading \u2014 H1 through H6. Headings are auto-anchored so the auto side-nav can link to them.
  • PageNav \u2014 renders the tree of children of the current or a specified page, with an optional search box.
  • Published \u2014 a callout with the last-reviewed / next-review dates.
  • Rich text \u2014 TinyMCE-authored HTML, sanitised on save against the GOV.UK-safe allow-list.
  • Search \u2014 a search box scoped to a subtree of the page tree.
  • Summary list \u2014 GDS key / value summary rows.
"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Region layouts"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Each region carries a layout that maps to the GOV.UK grid: single, one-half-one-half, two-thirds-one-third, one-third-two-thirds, and thirds / quarters variants. Pick the layout that matches what your content wants; the editor renders the columns side by side so you can see how it will lay out at desktop widths.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Moving widgets"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Widgets can be dragged into any slot in any region on the page \u2014 including across columns and into new regions. The drop target shows an inflated placeholder so you can see exactly where the widget will land.

"}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: Content pages are built from a tree of regions containing widgets . A region is a horizontal band that can be split into columns; each column holds an ordered list of widgets. The editor at a glance The content editor. Regions have a light-orange background so you can see the layout while you edit. Adding a widget Every gap between widgets shows an inline Add content here button. Click it to open the widget picker. The palette lists widgets alphabetically: Card — title + body + optional image and link. Cards laid out in the same row auto-equalise height. Divider — a horizontal rule. Heading — H1 through H6. Headings are auto-anchored so the auto side-nav can link to them. PageNav — renders the tree of children of the current or a specified page, with an optional search box. Published — a callout with the last-reviewed / next-review dates. Rich text — TinyMCE-authored HTML, sanitised on save against the GOV.UK-safe allow-list. Search — a search box scoped to a subtree of the page tree. Summary list — GDS key / value summary rows. Region layouts Each region carries a layout that maps to the GOV.UK grid: single , one-half-one-half , two-thirds-one-third , one-third-two-thirds , and thirds / quarters variants. Pick the layout that matches what your content wants; the editor renders the columns side by side so you can see how it will lay out at desktop widths. Moving widgets Widgets can be dragged into any slot in any region on the page — including across columns and into new regions. The drop target shows an inflated placeholder so you can see exactly where the widget will land.

pageNodes.title: Drafts, versions, and publishing

versions.content:
[{"kind":"region","layout":"one-third-two-thirds","columns":[[{"kind":"widget","type":"pagenav","props":{"mode":"children","childrenParentPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-editors","showSearch":false,"searchPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-editors","searchLabel":"Search this section"}}],[{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Every save produces a new version. The page tracks a draft alongside its live version so an editor can iterate without disturbing the public site.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Draft vs. live"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

The status tag next to the page title tells you the current state at a glance: Draft, Live, or Past for versions whose publish window has ended. Draft versions use decimal numbers (1.1, 1.2 \u2026); when a draft is published, the whole-integer version increments (2.0 \u2026).

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Publish, schedule, unpublish"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Publish draft makes the current draft the live version immediately. If you fill in a publish window first, the button ignores the date and goes live now \u2014 that's a deliberate guard. To schedule for later, save the draft, fill in the start date on the version row, and let it flip automatically when the time arrives.

Unpublish takes the page off the public site immediately. The version rows are kept; publish again at any time.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Restoring an older version"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Every version row on the Versions tab has a Restore action. Restoring copies that version's content into a new draft, which you can then edit and publish. The original historical version is not modified \u2014 restore is non-destructive.

"}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: Every save produces a new version. The page tracks a draft alongside its live version so an editor can iterate without disturbing the public site. Draft vs. live The status tag next to the page title tells you the current state at a glance: Draft , Live , or Past for versions whose publish window has ended. Draft versions use decimal numbers (1.1, 1.2 …); when a draft is published, the whole-integer version increments (2.0 …). Versions tab: every historical version and the current publish state. Publish, schedule, unpublish Publish draft makes the current draft the live version immediately. If you fill in a publish window first, the button ignores the date and goes live now — that's a deliberate guard. To schedule for later, save the draft, fill in the start date on the version row, and let it flip automatically when the time arrives. Unpublish takes the page off the public site immediately. The version rows are kept; publish again at any time. Restoring an older version Every version row on the Versions tab has a Restore action. Restoring copies that version's content into a new draft, which you can then edit and publish. The original historical version is not modified — restore is non-destructive.

versions.content:
[{"kind":"region","layout":"one-third-two-thirds","columns":[[{"kind":"widget","type":"pagenav","props":{"mode":"children","childrenParentPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-editors","showSearch":false,"searchPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-editors","searchLabel":"Search this section"}}],[{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Content blocks are named snippets of HTML you can drop into templates (like the footer) or into pages. Editors change a block once; every page that references it re-renders.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Finding content blocks"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Go to Content blocks in the admin sidebar. The tree mirrors the pages tree, but pruned to pages that actually own a block \u2014 so a block's admin location matches the page it renders on.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Editing a block"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Click any block to open its editor. Changes are versioned separately from the page's own version history \u2014 content blocks have their own history table with Revert against each row.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Auto-provisioning"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

When a template references a block that doesn't exist yet (the footer's Support and guidance section is an example), the page renders using the template's default HTML and the block is created behind the scenes on that first render. It then appears in the content-blocks tree ready to be edited.

"}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: Content blocks are named snippets of HTML you can drop into templates (like the footer) or into pages. Editors change a block once; every page that references it re-renders. Finding content blocks Go to Content blocks in the admin sidebar. The tree mirrors the pages tree, but pruned to pages that actually own a block — so a block's admin location matches the page it renders on. Content blocks admin: pruned to pages that reference a block. Editing a block Click any block to open its editor. Changes are versioned separately from the page's own version history — content blocks have their own history table with Revert against each row. Auto-provisioning When a template references a block that doesn't exist yet (the footer's Support and guidance section is an example), the page renders using the template's default HTML and the block is created behind the scenes on that first render. It then appears in the content-blocks tree ready to be edited.

versions.bodyPlainText: Reorder + reparent by dragging In the admin left nav, grab any page and drag it. A placeholder slot inflates between siblings to show exactly where the page will land. Release to drop. Reparenting works the same way — drag onto a folder to make it a child. After a move, the tree opens to the moved page's new location so you keep your bearings. Right-click context menu Right-click any node for the full action list: Edit, Versions, New child page, Delete. Middle-click (or Ctrl-click) on Edit, Versions, or New child opens in a new tab. Deleted pages Deleting a page soft-deletes it — the row and its versions are kept. Deleted pages live at /admin/pages/deleted . Restore any row to bring it back with its whole version history intact.

pageNodes.title: Importing and exporting content

versions.content:
[{"kind":"region","layout":"one-third-two-thirds","columns":[[{"kind":"widget","type":"pagenav","props":{"mode":"children","childrenParentPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-administrators","showSearch":false,"searchPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-administrators","searchLabel":"Search this section"}}],[{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Content staging exports the page tree and content blocks as a JSON bundle you can re-import into another environment. Everything is matched by stable GUID identity, with a path/key fallback so a bundle importing into a partially-seeded env adopts the local roots rather than colliding.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Exporting"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Export everything downloads the whole tree and every block. Choose what to export opens a catalog where you can tick specific pages and blocks \u2014 ancestor pages are added automatically so the tree stays consistent.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Importing"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Upload a bundle to see the preview. The wizard always shows the same shape:

  • Default for new items \u2014 Include (default) or Skip. Choose Skip to opt out of new content by default and pick a subset via per-item radios.
  • Default for items already in this environment \u2014 Skip (default), Overwrite, or Fail. Only enabled when the bundle contains colliding items.

Both tables have per-item action radios (Use default / Include / Skip / Overwrite) so you can override individual items \u2014 pick a two-page subset of a 36-page bundle by setting Skip as the default and marking just the two rows Include.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Clear all CMS content"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

The red button at the bottom of the staging page truncates every page and content block, then lets the startup seeders regenerate the default root nodes. Use it to reset a test environment before replaying a bundle. Behind a confirm modal \u2014 you have to explicitly type Yes, clear everything.

"}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: Content staging exports the page tree and content blocks as a JSON bundle you can re-import into another environment. Everything is matched by stable GUID identity, with a path/key fallback so a bundle importing into a partially-seeded env adopts the local roots rather than colliding. Content staging landing page. Exporting Export everything downloads the whole tree and every block. Choose what to export opens a catalog where you can tick specific pages and blocks — ancestor pages are added automatically so the tree stays consistent. Importing Upload a bundle to see the preview. The wizard always shows the same shape: Default for new items — Include (default) or Skip. Choose Skip to opt out of new content by default and pick a subset via per-item radios. Default for items already in this environment — Skip (default), Overwrite, or Fail. Only enabled when the bundle contains colliding items. Both tables have per-item action radios (Use default / Include / Skip / Overwrite) so you can override individual items — pick a two-page subset of a 36-page bundle by setting Skip as the default and marking just the two rows Include. Clear all CMS content The red button at the bottom of the staging page truncates every page and content block, then lets the startup seeders regenerate the default root nodes. Use it to reset a test environment before replaying a bundle. Behind a confirm modal — you have to explicitly type Yes, clear everything .

The role settings grid is the source of truth for which role sees which admin section. Columns are roles; rows are sections (CMS administration, System administration, Storage, and so on). Tick to grant.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"The Admin column is locked"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Admin is granted every section by default and the checkboxes are read-only. The server-side handler forces the Admin row to be the full set on every save regardless of what the form contained \u2014 so the admin can never lose access by accident.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Adding a role"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Type a role name into the Add role input and save. The new role appears as a column with no grants \u2014 tick sections and save again to grant. A sentinel row keeps the empty role registered so it persists in the DB until you add real grants.

"}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: The role settings grid is the source of truth for which role sees which admin section. Columns are roles; rows are sections (CMS administration, System administration, Storage, and so on). Tick to grant. Role settings grid. Admin is locked to every section — you cannot revoke. The Admin column is locked Admin is granted every section by default and the checkboxes are read-only. The server-side handler forces the Admin row to be the full set on every save regardless of what the form contained — so the admin can never lose access by accident. Adding a role Type a role name into the Add role input and save. The new role appears as a column with no grants — tick sections and save again to grant. A sentinel row keeps the empty role registered so it persists in the DB until you add real grants.

pageNodes.title: Viewing application logs

versions.content:
[{"kind":"region","layout":"one-third-two-thirds","columns":[[{"kind":"widget","type":"pagenav","props":{"mode":"children","childrenParentPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-administrators","showSearch":false,"searchPath":"help/how-to-use-the-cms/for-administrators","searchLabel":"Search this section"}}],[{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Every ILogger event at Information level or above (Warning, Error, Critical) is written to a Postgres table and surfaced under System administration \u2192 View logs. Nothing to install; no separate log aggregator to check.

"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Filtering"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Filter by:

  • Level \u2014 Information, Warning, Error, Critical.
  • Category \u2014 the logger source, e.g. ContentStagingService.
  • Date range \u2014 From / To in UTC.
  • Search \u2014 free-text match against the message or the exception (case-insensitive).
"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":""}},{"kind":"widget","type":"heading","props":{"level":2,"text":"Download and clear"}},{"kind":"widget","type":"richtext","props":{"html":"

Download CSV streams the current filter row-by-row so a large log table doesn't blow memory. Clear all logs truncates the table (behind a confirm modal); new events continue to be recorded from the next request onward.

"}}]]}]
versions.bodyPlainText: Every ILogger event at Information level or above (Warning, Error, Critical) is written to a Postgres table and surfaced under System administration → View logs. Nothing to install; no separate log aggregator to check. View logs. Newest events first; page size follows the shared rows-per-page setting. Filtering Filter by: Level — Information, Warning, Error, Critical. Category — the logger source, e.g. ContentStagingService . Date range — From / To in UTC. Search — free-text match against the message or the exception (case-insensitive). Filtering on the ContentStagingService category isolates every log from a specific service. Download and clear Download CSV streams the current filter row-by-row so a large log table doesn't blow memory. Clear all logs truncates the table (behind a confirm modal); new events continue to be recorded from the next request onward.

pageNodes.subtitle: Every ILogger event, in the database, searchable in the browser.
